title: Strict scalar-unit pairings before the open projection comparison
statement: Under the site, ring, universe and sheafification hypotheses of def-sf-open-tensor-scalar-unit-data, every strict inverse system A of unital commutative R-algebra sheaves admits StrictTotals and natural chain maps cT and cS from the constant source and slice-source towers. Their values on homogeneous pure generators insert the scalar 1 into each of the two scalar-extension factors. The transitions send each of the two coefficient entries through the prescribed coefficient ring map. This asserts neither an open comparison isomorphism nor an augmentation square.

proof.text: We use the sheaf tensor universal property and bilinear sheafification uniqueness, not surjectivity on sections. A map from $j_{B!}M\otimes_BN$ is determined by $[x]_f\otimes y$: compare the two associated bilinear pairings after precomposition by $P_M\times N$; the formulas agree on each summand, hence on finite sums, and uniqueness of bilinear extension and the tensor universal property give equality. For the iterated source $((j_{B!}M)\otimes_B A_n)\otimes_{A_n}(N\otimes_B A_n)$, apply the tensor universal property first to the outer tensor, then to each inner tensor, and the same bilinear-extension uniqueness to $P_M$. It suffices to test $([x]_f\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ for original sections over each $W$. On the slice the same argument omits $P_M$. These are repeated universal-property applications. Finally a map from a total direct sum is determined by its summand composites. Extension $j_{B!}$ preserves these sums since it is a left adjoint; the discrete indexing sets $\{(p,q):p+q=d\}$ are small. Thus these tests apply degreewise also to extended totals.

proof.text: For any $B$-module sheaf $M$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$ is a $B$-linear map to the underlying $B$-module of $M\otimes_BA_n$: $(cs)\otimes1=s\otimes c=c(s\otimes1)$. It commutes with restrictions. The pairing $(s,y)\mapsto(s\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes1)$ is $B$-bilinear, so the sheaf tensor universal property defines the degreewise $c_{T,n}$; use $s=[x]_f$ for the stated formula. The identical construction over $B_V$ defines $c_{S,n}$. The restriction tensor comparison identifies $j^*(y\otimes1)$ with $j^*y\otimes1$. For $x$ in degree $p$ and $y$ in degree $q$, both the differential after augmentation and the augmentation after differential are the sum of the terms obtained by replacing $x$ with $dx$ and by replacing $y$ with $dy$, the second multiplied by $(-1)^p$. Thus these maps totalize to chain maps. A transition $q_{m,n}$ takes each inserted $1$ to $1$; hence both components commute with every transition and define the asserted maps out of constant strict towers. Identity and composition of transitions follow from $q_{n,n}=1$ and $q_{l,n}=q_{m,n}q_{l,m}$ on each coefficient factor.
